summary: 皮亚杰通过观察和访谈追问儿童怎样建构知识。孩子对“风是怎么来的”的解释，显示了儿童自己的推理体系，也引出了对发展阶段及其教育意义的讨论。

paragraphs.brief: 爱因斯坦称之为“一个简单到只有天才才会想到的发现”。
sentences: Jean Piaget spent much of his professional life listening to children, watching children and poring over reports of researchers around the world who were doing the same.
让·皮亚格特在职业生涯中花了很多时间倾听儿童的声音，关注儿童，并报道世界各地研究人员也这样做的报告。
He found, to put it most succinctly, that children don’t think like grown-ups.
他发现，最简洁地说，孩子们不象成年人那样思考。

After thousands of interactions with young people often barely old enough to talk, Piaget began to suspect that behind their cute and seemingly irrational utterances were thought processes that had their own kind of order and their own special logic.
皮雅特在与年轻人进行数千次互动后，往往年纪不大，无法说话。皮雅格特开始怀疑，在他们可爱的、似乎不合理的言论背后，认为过程有他们自己的秩序和特殊逻辑。
Einstein called it “a discovery so simple that only a genius could have thought of it.”
爱因斯坦称之为“一个简单到只有天才才会想到的发现”。

paragraphs.brief: Piget虽然不是教育改革者，却倡导一种思考儿童的方式，为今天的教育改革运动奠定了基础。
sentences: Although not an educational reformer, Piaget championed a way of thinking about children that provided the foundation for today’s education-reform movements.
Piget虽然不是教育改革者，却倡导一种思考儿童的方式，为今天的教育改革运动奠定了基础。
It was a shift comparable to the way modern anthropology displaced stories of primitive tribes being ‘noble savages’ and ‘cannibals’.
与现代人类学转移原始部落为“无名野蛮人”和“cannibals”的故事相似。
One might say that Piaget was the first to take children’s thinking seriously.
皮雅格特是第一个认真对待儿童思想的人。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然他可能没有比西格蒙德·弗洛伊德甚至B·F·斯金纳那么出名但他对心理学的影响可能更持久
sentences: He has been revered by generations of teachers inspired by the belief that children are not empty vessels to be filled with knowledge (as traditional pedagogical theory had it) but active builders of knowledge—little scientists who are constantly creating and testing their own hypotheses about the world.
他受到几代教师的尊敬，他们认为，儿童不是空洞的容器，可以填满知识(如传统教学理论那样)，而是知识的积极建设者，这些小科学家不断创造和测试他们自己关于世界的假设。
And though he may not be as famous as Sigmund Freud or even B. F. Skinner, his influence on psychology may be longer lasting.
虽然他可能没有比西格蒙德·弗洛伊德甚至B·F·斯金纳那么出名但他对心理学的影响可能更持久

paragraphs.brief: 皮亚杰从儿童答错题目的共同模式出发，用访谈追问他们如何推理。朱莉娅用树枝摇动解释风从哪里来。
sentences: In 1920, while doing research in a child-psychology laboratory in Paris, Piaget noticed that children of the same age made similar errors on intelligence tests.
1920年，Piaget在巴黎的一个儿童心理实验室进行研究时注意到，同龄儿童在智力测试上也犯了类似的错误。
Fascinated by their reasoning processes, he began to suspect that the key to human knowledge might be discovered by observing how the child’s mind develops.
他对他们的推理过程感到困惑，开始怀疑，通过观察儿童的心智发展，人类知识的关键可能被发现。
On his return to Switzerland he began watching children play, scrupulously recording their words and actions as their minds raced to find reasons for why things are the way they are.
回到瑞士后，他开始观看儿童玩耍，认真记录他们的言行，因为他们的心急着寻找为什么事情是这样的原因。
In one of his most famous experiments, Piaget asked children, ‘What makes the wind?’
Piget在他的最著名的实验之一中问孩子们：「风是什么？
A typical dialogue would be:
典型的对话是：
Piaget: What makes the wind?
皮亚杰：风是怎么来的？
Julia: The trees.
朱莉娅：是树弄出来的。
Piaget: How do you know?
皮亚杰：你怎么知道？
Julia: I saw them waving their arms.
朱莉娅：我看见它们挥动手臂了。
Piaget: How does that make the wind?
皮亚杰：挥动手臂怎么会起风呢？
Julia (waving her hand in front of his face): Like this.
朱莉娅（在他面前挥了挥手）：就像这样。
Only they are bigger.
只不过树比我大。
And there are lots of trees.
而且树有好多棵。

paragraphs.brief: Piget承认，5岁的Julia的信仰，尽管按任何成人标准来看都并不正确，但也不`错误 '。
sentences: Piaget recognised that five-year-old Julia’s beliefs, while not correct by any adult criterion, are not ‘incorrect’ either.
Piget承认，5岁的Julia的信仰，尽管按任何成人标准来看都并不正确，但也不`错误 '。
They are entirely sensible and coherent within the framework of the child’s way of knowing.
在儿童了解的方式框架内，这些方法完全合理和一致。
Classifying them as ‘true’ or ‘false’ misses the point and shows a lack of respect for the child.
将她们归类为“真”或“假”，忽略了这一点，并显示出对孩子缺乏尊重。

What Piaget was after was a theory that the wind dialogue demonstrated coherence, ingenuity and the practice of a kind of explanatory principle (in this case by referring to body actions) that stands young children in very good stead when they don’t know enough or don’t have enough skill to handle the kind of explanation that grown-ups prefer.
Piaget所追求的是一个理论，即风力对话显示了一致性、才智和实践，这是一种解释性原则(这里指的是身体行为)，在幼儿不了解或没有足够的技能处理成年人喜欢的那种解释时，这种解释性原则代表着他们。

paragraphs.brief: 正如皮雅格特所说，“儿童只真正了解他们自己发明的东西，每次我们试图太快地教他们一些东西，我们就阻止他们自己发明。
sentences: Piaget was not an educator and never laid down rules about how to intervene in such situations.
Piget不是教育者，从未规定如何干预这种情况的规则。
But his work strongly suggests that the automatic reaction of putting the child right may well be counter-productive.
但是，他的工作强烈地表明，将儿童权利放在一边的自动反应很可能适得其反。
If their theories are always greeted by ‘Nice try, but this is how it really is…’ they might give up after a while on making theories.
如果他们的理论总是被"不错的尝试，但这就是它是如何真实的..." 他们可能会放弃一段时间后，编造理论。

As Piaget put it, ‘children have real understanding only of that which they invent themselves, and each time that we try to teach them something too quickly, we keep them from inventing it themselves.’
正如皮雅格特所说，“儿童只真正了解他们自己发明的东西，每次我们试图太快地教他们一些东西，我们就阻止他们自己发明。

paragraphs.brief: 皮雅格特的异见人士对孩子的原始物理定律有容忍之心：当他们看不到东西时，东西就会消失；月亮和太阳会跟着你；大东西会漂浮，小东西会沉没。
sentences: Disciples of Piaget have a tolerance for—indeed a fascination with—children’s primitive laws of physics: that things disappear when they are out of sight; that the moon and the sun follow you around; that big things float and small things sink.
皮雅格特的异见人士对孩子的原始物理定律有容忍之心：当他们看不到东西时，东西就会消失；月亮和太阳会跟着你；大东西会漂浮，小东西会沉没。

Einstein was intrigued by Piaget’s findings, especially by the idea that seven-year-olds insist that going faster can take more time—perhaps because this, like Einstein’s own theories of relativity, runs so contrary to common sense.
爱因斯坦对皮雅格特的发现很感兴趣，特别是7岁的孩子坚持说更快的前进需要更多的时间 — — 也许是因为这和爱因斯坦自己的相对论一样，与常识背道而驰。

paragraphs.brief: 虽然每一位受训教师仍回忆起皮亚热的童年发展历程，但皮亚热工作的很大一部分却不太为人所知，也许是因为教育学校认为这对教师来说“太深了”。
sentences: Although every teacher in training still memorises Piaget’s successive stages of childhood development, the greater part of Piaget’s work is less well known, perhaps because schools of education regard it as ‘too deep’ for teachers.
虽然每一位受训教师仍回忆起皮亚热的童年发展历程，但皮亚热工作的很大一部分却不太为人所知，也许是因为教育学校认为这对教师来说“太深了”。
Piaget never thought of himself as a child psychologist.
皮亚格特从未把自己当儿童心理学家
His real interest was epistemology—the theory of knowledge—which, like physics, was considered a branch of philosophy until Piaget came along and made it a science.
他真正感兴趣的是认知学——知识理论——与物理学一样，在皮雅格特出现并使之成为科学之前，它被视为哲学的一个分支。

paragraphs.brief: Piget通过认知学探索了多种了解方式。
sentences: Through epistemology, Piaget explored multiple ways of knowing.
Piget通过认知学探索了多种了解方式。
He acknowledged them and examined them non-judgementally, yet with a philosopher’s analytic rigour.
他承认了这些结论，并用非判断性的方式审查了这些结论，但哲学家却以分析的严谨态度审查了这些结论。
Since Piaget, the territory has been widely colonised by those who write about women’s ways of knowing, Afrocentric ways of knowing, even the computer’s ways of knowing.
自皮雅格特以来，领土被那些写了妇女了解、以非洲为中心的了解方式，甚至计算机了解方式的人广泛殖民。
Indeed, artificial intelligence and the information-processing model of the mind owe more to Piaget than its proponents may realise.
事实上，人造智慧和思想的信息处理模式对Piaget的帮助大于其支持者可能意识到的。

paragraphs.brief: 皮雅格特的核心是，他认为仔细研究儿童知识的发展方式将阐明知识的一般性质。
sentences: The core of Piaget is his belief that looking carefully at how knowledge develops in children will elucidate the nature of knowledge in general.
皮雅格特的核心是，他认为仔细研究儿童知识的发展方式将阐明知识的一般性质。
Whether this has in fact led to deeper understanding remains, like everything about Piaget, controversial.
这是否实际上导致更深入的理解，与Piaget的所有事情一样，仍然有争议。
In the past decade, Piaget has been vigorously challenged by the current fashion of viewing knowledge as an intrinsic property of the brain.
在过去十年中，Piget一直受到目前将知识视为大脑固有特性的强烈挑战。
Ingenious experiments have demonstrated that newborn infants already have some of the knowledge that Piaget believed children constructed.
巧妙的实验表明，新生婴儿已经掌握了皮雅格特认为儿童所建造的一些知识。

But for those, like me, who still see Piaget as the giant in the field of cognitive theory, the difference between what the baby brings and what the adult has is so immense that the new discoveries do not significantly reduce the gap, but only increase the mystery.
但对于像我一样仍然把皮雅格特看成认知理论领域的巨人的人来说婴儿带来的和成年人所拥有的差别是如此之大以至于新的发现不会显著缩小差距反而只会增加神秘感

items.en: In the second paragraph, the writer mentions the example of modern anthropology to illustrate
items.zh: 在第二段中，作者提到现代人类学的例子，以说明
correct: how Piaget’s work represents a crucial turning-point in our approach to education.
Piget的工作如何代表着我们教育方法的关键转折点。

items.en: According to the writer, what point is illustrated by the dialogue about the wind?
items.zh: 据作者说，关于风的对话说明了什么问题？
correct: The factual accuracy of what children say is of minor significance.
儿童所说的事实准确性并不重要。

items.en: Piaget believed in the importance of
correct: maintaining children’s confidence in their ability to interpret the world.
保持儿童对其理解世界的能力的信心。

items.en: What does the writer suggest in the seventh paragraph?
items.zh: 作者在第七段有什么建议？
correct: Even apparently irrational ideas can be worthy of interest.
即使是显然不理智的想法也值得关注。

items.en: The writer’s main purpose is to
correct: outline Piaget’s contribution to a range of scientific fields.
概要介绍皮阿吉特对一系列科学领域的贡献。

items.en: Piaget maintained that children’s mental processes were far more ________ than they might appear.
items.zh: 皮亚杰认为，儿童的思维过程远比表面看上去更 ________。
items.why: 皮亚杰认为儿童思维比表面看上去更“有逻辑"。

items.en: He encouraged the view that a child was not a ‘blank slate’ waiting to be filled with information, but rather a systematic builder of knowledge who regularly tries out his or her own ________ about the world.
items.zh: 在皮亚杰看来，儿童会有系统地主动建构知识，经常检验自己对世界的 ________，并非一块等着别人填入信息的“白板”。
items.why: 孩子反复验证的是自己的“理论”。

items.en: Piaget’s impact on the area of ________ could well outlast that of more celebrated pioneers of this discipline.
items.zh: 皮亚杰对 ________ 领域的影响，很可能比该学科中一些名气更大的先驱更持久。
items.why: 影响最大的学科领域被明确指出是“心理学”。

items.en: Despite doubts cast over his ideas by the current view associating knowledge exclusively with the ________, the effects of his work are still strong today.
items.zh: 如今有一种观点把知识完全归于 ________，因而有人质疑皮亚杰的看法。即便如此，他的工作至今仍有很大影响。
items.why: 质疑声音将知识归因于“大脑",与皮亚杰形成对比。

items.en: His principles are still widely used in the professional development of ________.
items.zh: 他的原则至今仍广泛用于 ________ 的在职培训。
items.why: 皮亚杰原理仍广泛用于教师的职业发展。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

items.en: Piaget’s early work in Paris involved innovative research techniques.
items.zh: Piget在巴黎的早期工作涉及创新研究技术。
items.why: 在巴黎的实验室，皮亚杰发现同龄儿童常在智力测试中犯相似的错误。这里写的是他的观察发现，没有评价当时采用的研究方法是否创新。

items.en: Piaget gave clear guidelines as to how adults should give information to children.
items.zh: Piget就成年人应如何向儿童提供信息提供了明确的指导方针。
items.why: 作者明确说皮亚杰没有给出成人应如何授课的明确指导。

items.en: Piaget made a significant contribution to the field of epistemology.
items.zh: Piget对认知学领域作出了重大贡献。
items.why: 皮亚杰用认识论研究多种认识方式，后来许多研究者继续拓展了这一领域。后继研究的扩展说明他的工作产生了重要影响。

items.en: We still have much to learn about the nature of knowledge.
items.zh: 我们仍然有很多关于知识性质的知识。
items.why: 作者认为关于知识本质仍有许多未知。

两种说法都比较影响延续的时间，也都保留了推测语气。

皮亚杰原理仍广泛用于教师的职业发展。

连接词 after 引出“After thousands of interactions with young people often barely old enough to talk”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 after 把这一层关系补进去。
“that Piaget was the first to take children’s thinking seriously”补足 say 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 say 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

西摩·帕普特研究瑞士哲学家和心理学家的工作
